issue_context.title: Prerendering fails if file-based routing is disabled, but there are .vue files in pages directory
issue_context.body:
### Environment

- Operating System: Linux
- Node Version:     v18.18.0
- Nuxt Version:     3.10.0
- CLI Version:      3.10.0
- Nitro Version:    2.8.1
- Package Manager:  npm@10.2.3
- Builder:          -
- User Config:      devtools
- Runtime Modules:  -
- Build Modules:    -

### Reproduction

https://stackblitz.com/edit/nuxt-starter-sgbtc2

```shell
npm run generate
```

### Describe the bug

During prerendering, it tries to pre-render pages corresponding to `.vue` files in `/pages` directory, but since the server is responding with 404 status code, the whole process fails.

This can be cured by adding all the pseudo-routes to `nitro.prerender.ignore` array of nuxt config file.

### Additional context

_No response_

### Logs

_No response_
comments: _Start a new pull request in [StackBlitz Codeflow](https://stackblitz.com/~/github.com/nuxt/nuxt/issues/25594?repros=nuxt-starter-sgbtc2)._ - [**nuxt-starter-sgbtc2** (Open reproduction)](https://stackblitz.com/edit/nuxt-starter-sgbtc2?issueRepo=nuxt/nuxt&issueNumber=25594)
I'd be happy to take a look at this

It seems nitro is being handed the wrong route options when prerendering here https://github.com/nuxt/nuxt/blob/ec5d254f417d04e92acd0a716c662637e178f6a6/packages/nuxt/src/core/nitro.ts#L501

I'm debugging further

The prerender config is set by [this line](https://github.com/nuxt/nuxt/blob/fa79b86d4ab286c3c43735b5d589006e95d9182f/packages/nuxt/src/pages/module.ts#L281) which sets it to a set of pages from [created only from pages within the `/pages` directory](https://github.com/nuxt/nuxt/blob/fa79b86d4ab286c3c43735b5d589006e95d9182f/packages/nuxt/src/pages/module.ts#L258).

The custom `router.options.ts` seems only imported by the runtime code generated by [this template](https://github.com/nuxt/nuxt/blob/fa79b86d4ab286c3c43735b5d589006e95d9182f/packages/nuxt/src/pages/module.ts#L442).

I see now that the pages module doesn't have the final routing config in memory when creating the prerendering config.

I see a few ways to tackle this. Let me know if there are others.
1. Import the `router.options.ts` file (and any other files) in the pages module to discover what the final routing config resolves to.
    - Is there precedent for something similar elsewhere in nuxt? I haven't found anything yet, but I'll keep looking.
2. Change the way prerendering works to introspect the running site to discover what routes exist.
    - Based on what I know about nitro and nuxt thus far, this seems like it would require a change to nitro and the generated app for prerendering. I could be wrong though.

@danielroe any thoughts?

I think we should use a Nuxt plugin that is guarded by `import.meta.prerender` so it does not add anything to the final build, and which only executes once, passing all paths to the `prerenderRoutes` composable.

(this would only be if `ssr: true`)

Just to make sure we are talking about the same piece of code, you're referring to [this composable](https://github.com/nuxt/nuxt/blob/27f9c55fc2f5c7d6a21920e6bd902a7ebc728efc/packages/nuxt/src/app/composables/ssr.ts#L62) correct?

Also, I'll be happy to take this on if you want to assign it to me.

Hey, thank you for taking your time into resolving this issue, but unfortunately it is still not fixed in the latest Nuxt version (3.12.4). You can use the same reproduction to confirm that (since nuxt has a ^ before the version, it will install the newer version and then run `npm run generate`): https://stackblitz.com/edit/nuxt-starter-sgbtc2).

review_comments:
Is there anything that preserves the `nuxt.options.dev` or `nitro.options.static` guards?

I'm guessing the `.server.ts` extension serves the purpose of `nuxt.options.dev`.
This condition plus nitro not scanning `/` by default means the pages directory routes are no longer prerendered automatically. Was this intentional?
Under what circumstances would this be run more than once?
